canonical_spec.title: Financial intermediation and bank economics
canonical_spec.outcome: Explain the economic functions and fragilities of financial intermediaries.

assignments.scope: Financial intermediation as a response to screening, monitoring, contracting and payment needs; explicit original incentive/cost example rather than labels. Teach deposit/loan balance-sheet creation, income/spread/cost versus capital, maturity transformation and a coherent simple liquidity-insurance/run mechanism with stated information and liquidation rights. Delimit preliminary run treatment from Chapter5 deeper liquidity. Link accepted monetary/accounting/investment/derivatives tools. Do not claim deposits mechanically fund every new loan or that profitable lending precludes cash fragility.

canonical_spec.title: Bank balance sheets, capital and liquidity
canonical_spec.outcome: Reconcile bank accounts and distinguish liquidity shortages from insolvency.

assignments.scope: Reconcile original bank balance-sheet and income transactions, loss provisions/charge-offs/cash and capital; distinguish book and economic value, leverage versus risk-weighted capital concepts, encumbrance/haircut and dated liquidity capacity. Build one consistent bank ledger and independent stress reconciliation. Distinguish capital/accounting measures from deployable cash. Any actual regulatory definition requires dated primary source and jurisdiction; invented thresholds remain explicitly instructional; full regulatory architecture belongs in Chapter9.

canonical_spec.title: Credit analysis and lending decisions
canonical_spec.outcome: Evaluate creditworthiness using cash flow, incentives and downside protection.

assignments.scope: Evaluate an original corporate borrower using operating cash/debt service, leverage and covenant definitions, primary repayment sources, collateral recovery timing and seniority, underwriting incentives and downside stress. Distinguish borrower project value, lender debt payoff, accounting profit and cash debt service; distinguish physical repayment scenarios from Q pricing law. Teach a complete defensible approval/restructure/refusal example and evidence/monitoring/remediation, with complete determinate solutions and open rubrics.

canonical_spec.title: Market risk and portfolio loss
canonical_spec.outcome: Compare risk measures and state their information and distributional limitations.

assignments.scope: Loss sign/horizon/physical information, left quantile VaR, probability atoms and tail-average expected shortfall; original finite tail/dual/minimization and coherence proof, VaR non-subadditivity, dependence stress, explicit normal/horizon limitations, heavy tails, full revaluation versus approximation, exception-count/backtesting limits and severity/coverage distinction. Use existing bounded standard-library tools; no claim risk metrics equal capital requirements or cover all losses.
